investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T16:45–16:53Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes (those matching the pod's node affinity/selector), and the 4 remaining nodes were excluded by that same affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 mismatched nodes. The result is a hard scheduling deadlock that prevented all three remote-agent checks from progressing past pod creation, leaving the expected-output contract entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" for every remote-agent pod creation attempt during the eval window. The two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining VM slots, and preemption was not possible. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T16:45–16:53Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes (those matching the pod's node affinity/selector), and the 4 remaining nodes were excluded by that same affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 mismatched nodes. The result is a hard scheduling deadlock that prevented all three remote-agent checks from progressing past pod creation, leaving the expected-output contract entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Swarm Nodes Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes swarm was left unscheduled: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never received an agent, and zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned, causing a complete contract violation.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes (0/2 available), and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. This prevents any remote agent pod from being scheduled, so the createAgent call in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918) never completes, no evidence is collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote agent swarm; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing agent pods, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — Node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible for remote agent pods. If those 2 nodes are at capacity, the cluster has zero scheduling headroom regardless of total node count.

TERTIARY — Leaked or zombie agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) failed to release VM resources from a previous run, slots may be held by stale pods, reducing available capacity for new evals.
